title: Philadelphia student analysed 600+ works and found Mozart less predictable
content: Eighteen-year-old Linus Chen-Plotkin from Philadelphia has created a groundbreaking study on the genius of Mozart. Using statistical tests to evaluate melody predictability, he found that Mozart's music demonstrated significantly lower predictability than that of his contemporaries. This unique characteristic allowed him to both adhere to classical standards and surprise his audience, offering fresh insights into the nature of musical innovation and the essence of artistic excellence.

title: Blind man escaped 9/11 by walking down 78 flights with help from guide dog

In the aftermath, Hingson found solace through sharing their powerful story of trust and collaboration.

title: Why archaeologists keep finding ancient cities beneath modern ones
content: Throughout history, ancient cities were frequently reconstructed at the same sites due to their inherent strategic benefits. Such locations provided essential resources like water, access to trade routes, and fertile land, which were valued across generations. As populations expanded, they built upon the existing infrastructure, resulting in the formation of layered urban landscapes. This progression naturally elevated ground levels over centuries, causing ancient remnants to lie beneath contemporary urban settings.
